links.outcome: Surgeon identification time and confidence with versus without AI assistance, by experience level
links.effect: Novices: median identification time 263 vs 390 frames (AI-on vs AI-off; P<0.001), confidence 4 vs 3 (P<0.001). Experts: 186 vs 172 frames (P=0.22), confidence 5 vs 5 (P=0.031).
links.quote: Among novices, median identification time was 263 (190-453) vs. 390 (272-555) frames (AI-on vs. AI-off; P < 0.001), and confidence was 4 (4-5) vs. 3 (3-4) (P < 0.001).

links.outcome: AI versus expert and novice surgeon TEF identification time in clip-based testing
links.effect: AI identified the TEF faster than experts and novices (1.05 s vs 2.87 s and 6.92 s).
links.quote: In clip-based testing, AI identified the TEF faster than experts and novices (1.05 versus 2.87 and 6.92 s).

screen.reason: The study evaluates a surgical video segmentation tool both in reader studies comparing surgeon performance with and without AI assistance, and via real-time deployment during actual operations.

primary.practice: real-time AI assistance / overlay during surgery
